completion_data.completion_summary: Produced a design specification resolving all 8 gaps (G1-G8) for routing confirmed email-cleanup decisions into sender/domain-aggregated memory-vault preferences, with the identity-normalization key empirically verified against a real read-only email-classify sample (2128 messages, 751 senders) rather than shipped provisional-unverified, plus two hand-authored ROADMAP.md entries and an explicit 822 scope recommendation.

memory_candidates.content: email-classify --emit-tagged is genuinely read-only (verified: no notmuch tag call, wrapper-contracts.md sec10a) and can be used to pull real sender/manifest data for design-time verification without mutating the live mailbox, as long as prior +proposed-* tags already exist from earlier classify passes (check with `notmuch count 'tag:proposed-delete or tag:proposed-archive or tag:proposed-unsure or tag:proposed-keep'` first). Prefer this over the provisional-unverified fallback when email-census/email-classify are on $PATH.

memory-retrieve.sh (the auto-retrieval script for /research, /plan, /implement) has no topic/namespace exclusion filter -- it scores corpus-wide by keyword overlap plus a topic/category bonus only. Any future reserved-namespace memory category (e.g. email/preferences/*) needs an explicit topic-prefix pre-filter added to the jq scoring block before it is safe from leaking into unrelated <memory-context> blocks.

No memory file in .memory/10-Memories/ currently uses a `category:` frontmatter field (verified: 0 of 19 files) -- the `category` seen in memory-index.json entries is synthesized from `tags` at index-build time, not read from real frontmatter. Any design proposing a schema-additive `category:` field should note this is a genuinely new mechanism, not an extension of an existing one.
